classification.difficultyReason: Apply the common-chord property, triangle angle sum and Pythagoras’ theorem to intersecting circles.

content.prompt: In the diagrams below, $P$ and $Q$ are the centres of the circles. Find the values of the variables.

spec.description: Intersecting circles with horizontal line of centres and vertical common chord. The upper half-chord is 6 cm, the distance from the chord to Q is 8 cm, the radius from Q to the upper intersection is y, and the lower triangle has angles x at P and 40° at the lower intersection. Decorative source colours and nonessential triangle shading are omitted.
spec.mathematics: The line of centres bisects the common chord at right angles. Coordinates use half-chord 6, distance from chord to Q 8, and distance from P to chord 6 tan(40°), preserving the stated angle and circle intersections.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and unknown labels appear; supplied answers are excluded.

answer.worked:
Let $M$ be the intersection of $PQ$ and the common chord. The line joining the centres bisects the common chord at right angles.

$$\begin{align*}x&=180^\circ-90^\circ-40^\circ\\x&=50^\circ\end{align*}$$

Using Pythagoras’ theorem in the right triangle with hypotenuse $y$:

$$\begin{align*}y^2&=6^2+8^2\\y^2&=100\\y&=10\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Two intersecting circles with centres Q and P. The vertical common chord passes through Q; its upper half is labelled 5 cm. The radius from P to the upper intersection is labelled 13 cm, and QP is labelled x. Ordinary geometry and labels use black.
spec.mathematics: The line of centres is perpendicular to the common chord. Coordinates form a right triangle with vertical leg 5 and hypotenuse 13; both circles pass through the common-chord endpoints.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the unknown x appear; the supplied answer is excluded.

answer.worked:
The line joining the centres is perpendicular to the common chord. Using Pythagoras’ theorem:

$$\begin{align*}x^2+5^2&=13^2\\x^2&=169-25\\x^2&=144\\x&=12\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
